before: Costimulation consists of additional supporting receptor interactions alongside antigen recognition, affecting activation, survival, division or differentiation. CD28 is one example, not the whole category or a universal threshold. The same peptide-HLA stimulus can receive different support without changing antigen specificity. Blocking inhibition and adding support are distinct interventions.

Measure division, cytokines and killing separately; marker abundance does not establish causal signalling. A schematic comparison can keep peptide-HLA recognition the same while adding support through CD28 in one condition. Showing no supporting contact in the other condition does not establish that its T cells lack CD28. Signal strength, duration, cell state, location and inhibitory context also shape the response. CTLA-4 can transfer CD80/CD86 from an opposing cell into the cell that carries CTLA-4 by trans-endocytosis, reducing the ligands available for CD28. Measure division, cytokines and killing under matched conditions. Neither this contact comparison nor ligand removal justifies eliminating every inhibitory input or establishes a universal response threshold.

before: Priming is a naive cell's initial activation in a supporting context. Signal one is TCR recognition of peptide-HLA, signal two includes CD80/CD86-CD28 costimulation and inhibitory context, and signal three includes differentiation-supporting cytokines. The receptor pre-exists the encounter. These signals interact over time; the model is not a three-button checklist and antigen-experienced or engineered cells can have different requirements.

IL-12 and type I interferons (alpha/beta) supported naive CD8 survival and cytolytic differentiation in defined experiments. Cytokines are signalling proteins, not nutritional fuel. Type I interferon can connect innate responses to priming, but this does not prescribe a universal cytokine intervention or establish every cGAS-STING step. Dendritic-cell priming support and tumour antigen display answer different questions.

Division, viable-cell expansion, cytokine production and target-cell death are distinct priming outcomes. In a fictional matched experiment both cultures show three divisions, yet only B kills appropriate targets above target-only background. Measure these outcomes separately with defined starting cells, presenting system, signal perturbation, matched time, peptide loading, HLA, cell ratios and culture conditions. Priming does not establish tumour access, natural display, safe killing or clinical benefit, and stronger stimulation can support unwanted populations.

In the schematic, peptide-HLA and supporting CD80/CD86 are on the presenter, while the naive T cell has its pre-existing TCR and CD28. In the fictional culture comparison, equal division with different killing shows a functional difference without identifying its cause. Testing a proposed cytokine explanation needs a controlled change in that signal while keeping viable-cell input, target identity and exposure comparable. Positive and negative controls help distinguish biological failure from assay failure. The three-signal categories organise the investigation; a division count alone does not diagnose a missing cytokine.
